A medical officer is urgently called to attend to a patient with critical injuries from a hit-and-run accident. As the patient's condition deteriorates rapidly, the medical officer considers recording the patient's account of the incident. Which is true for recording a dying declaration in India?

options.label: A
options.text: Medical officer must wait for the presence of the accused and their lawyer before recording the patient's statement.

options.label: B
options.text: Medical officer can record the patient's statement, but it is preferable for a magistrate to do so for it to be considered in court.

options.label: C
options.text: Medical officer is allowed to ask leading questions to quickly gather all necessary information from the patient.

options.label: D
options.text: If the patient unexpectedly recovers, their recorded statement will remain as the primary evidence in court proceedings.

questions.answerText: Medical officer can record the patient's statement, but it is preferable for a magistrate to do so for it to be considered in court.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Medical officer can record the patient's statement, but it is preferable for a magistrate to do so for it to be considered in court.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about scab formation in abrasions is correct in relation to the typical healing timeline?

options.label: A
options.text: Scab formation typically begins two days after an abrasion, occurring due to increased pressure at the wound site.

options.label: B
options.text: Scab formation typically begins 12 hours after an abrasion, occurring due to rapid tissue necrosis.

options.label: C
options.text: The scab itself is primarily composed of dried serum and coagulated blood proteins, which act as a protective barrier.

options.text: The scab will remain intact and unchanged for several days, even if healing is progressing well beneath it.

questions.answerText: The scab itself is primarily composed of dried serum and coagulated blood proteins, which act as a protective barrier.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) The scab itself is primarily composed of dried serum and coagulated blood proteins, which act as a protective barrier.
